title: Recursive vendor gjson::valid runs on client bodies outside deep_stack (process abort)
description:
Severity: critical (requires a valid client key).
Where: crates/cpa-server/src/codex_alpha.rs:42 (`routing(body)`, body up to 16 MiB), crates/cpa-server/src/websocket_requests.rs:355 (`previous_input`), crates/cpa-exec/src/codex_json.rs:65. Validator: vendor/gjson/src/valid.rs:85-202 (`valid_any` -> `valid_object`/`valid_array` -> `valid_any`, one frame per nesting level).

Claim: these sites call the vendored gjson validator, which recurses per nesting level, on client-controlled bodies with no sized stack. cpa-common's own `json::valid` (crates/cpa-common/src/json.rs:1758-1936) was made iterative for exactly this reason, but these callers use the vendor crate directly (cpa-server/Cargo.toml:27, cpa-exec/Cargo.toml:39).

Scenario: POST /backend-api/codex/alpha/... with a ~200 KB body of `[[[[...` -> ~200k frames on a 2 MiB tokio worker stack -> native stack overflow -> the whole proxy aborts (not a catchable panic). Go's gjson recurses the same way but on a growable goroutine stack.

Fix shape: route all three sites through `cpa_common::json::valid` (iterative, 10,000-level cap), or wrap them in `cpa_translate::deep_stack`. Grep for other direct `gjson::` uses on client input while there.

Windows: cargo check, fmt --check and clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings pass; workspace tests 1886 passed, the only failures are 35 that also fail at base 737ac93b plus 2 load-sensitive tests that pass alone. Iterative validators replace vendor gjson::valid on client input (codex_alpha.rs, websocket_requests.rs, websocket_tools.rs, codex_json.rs, codex_images.rs, codex_response.rs). Tests ok: deeply_nested_alpha_search_body_gets_the_invalid_body_answer, remarshal_rejects_deep_bodies_without_recursion.

title: gemini_schema repair_node deep-clones the subtree at every recursion level (O(n x depth))
description:
Severity: high (CPU DoS from one request; any client-key holder on a Gemini-family route).
Where: crates/cpa-common/src/gemini_schema.rs:598 (`node.clone()`), 628 (`props.clone()`), 789 (`child.clone()`), recursing at 661, 681, 708, 736, 764, 797. `GoValue::clone` is a deep clone; Go's `repairSchemaNode` copies the map shallowly.

Scenario: one tool schema {"properties":{"a":{"properties":{"a":...}}}} at the 10,000-level cap (~200 KB) -> on the order of 1e7..1e8 BTreeMap/String clones, seconds of CPU on a tokio worker, per schema, per request. Runs before `inline_refs` on every cleaner route.

Fix shape: take the node by value / mutate in place, or clone only the immediate map level as Go does. Add a benchmark-style test asserting linear growth.

title: Lease::drop and Completing::poll_next run fsync and an auth-dir walk on tokio worker threads
description:
Severity: high for deployments with save-cooldown-status and many accounts.
Where: crates/cpa-server/src/runtime.rs:1457-1461 (`Lease::drop` -> `report`) -> 2201-2288 (`record_model`) -> 2282-2286 calls `persist_cooldowns` and `persist_credential` synchronously. `persist_cooldowns` (1818-1844) -> cooldown_store::save (cooldown_store.rs:244-276) writes one file per credential with `write_bytes_atomic` (runtime.rs:3777-3809, `sync_all` on every write) and walks the whole auth-dir tree (`cds_files`, 194-210). `Completing::poll_next` (3871-3897) does the same via `lease.complete()` while holding the slot std::Mutex.

Scenario: 2,000 auth files, an upstream returning 429/5xx. Every failed attempt, every errored stream and every client disconnect performs a directory walk plus one or more fsyncs on whichever worker thread dropped the lease; concurrent failures serialise on `cooldown_write` (1822) and stall every other task on those workers.

Origin: Go persists in MarkResult too, but on a goroutine; the Rust port makes it a worker-thread stall.

Fix shape: hand the records to a single persister task (channel + spawn_blocking) and keep Drop non-blocking. Keep the write ordering guarantees the tests rely on.
notes: 2026-11-03T06:58:51Z decision: the per-result CREDENTIAL write stays synchronous in the recording call (as Go writes it); only the cooldown snapshot (one file per credential plus an auth-dir walk, the expensive part) goes to the coalescing persister thread. Deferring the credential write let a queued older write replace a newer edit on disk before the watcher reloaded it: runtime::tests::a_discarded_adopt_only_codex_refresh_changes_nothing and watching::tests::a_rewritten_token_clears_its_401_block_and_keeps_a_429 failed that way. The credential write runs once per revision (needs_persist), so it is rare on the request path. Test: a_recorded_result_writes_its_credential_in_the_same_call.

Cooldown snapshot moved to a coalescing persister thread; the per-result credential write stays in the recording call (see notes for why). Completing no longer holds its slot lock across completion. Tests ok: a_recorded_result_writes_its_credential_in_the_same_call, a_cooldown_reset_does_not_wait_for_its_save. Remaining callers moved in 7ea.48.

title: Git store writes ls-tree paths under the workspace without rejecting `..` or `.git` components
description:
Severity: high (requires a hostile or compromised GITSTORE remote).
Where: crates/cpa-store/src/git.rs:603-617 (`restore_missing`) and 552-584 (`reconcile`): `self.repo.join(path)` with paths from `git ls-tree -r -z --name-only HEAD` / `git diff --name-only -z`, no validation.

Scenario: the remote serves a tree containing `.git/config` or `../x`. `fetch.fsckObjects` is off by default so the objects arrive; git's own checkout refuses the path, so it is "missing"; `pull()` then calls `restore_missing()` which writes `.git/config` verbatim (core.fsmonitor / core.hooksPath / core.sshCommand -> command execution on the next git invocation) or a `..` path escapes the workspace root.

Origin: go-git's billy chroot blocks the `..` case, so that part is Rust-specific; whether Go shares the `.git/config` case is unverified.

Fix shape: reject any path with `..`, absolute, drive-prefixed, or a leading `.git` component before joining (the object store already has such a check at object.rs:536-547; reuse it), and consider `fetch.fsckObjects=true`.

title: sjson null-repeat padding driven by a numeric tool-schema property name (multi-GB allocation)
description:
Severity: high (requires a valid client key; any Gemini, Vertex, AI Studio or Antigravity route).
Where: crates/cpa-common/src/json.rs:2408-2419 (`append_build`) and 2539-2601 (`append_raw_paths`) emit `repeat(buf, b"null,", n)` with n from `atoui` when a missing path part is followed by a numeric part. Reached from crates/cpa-common/src/gemini_schema.rs:1541-1559 (`materialize_required_only_branch`: `set_raw(branch, "properties.<name>")` on a branch without `properties`) and 1414-1420 (`merge_conditionals`). `escape_key` escapes only `.`, `*` and `?`, so a purely numeric key is read as an array index.

Scenario: tool schema {"type":"object","properties":{"9999999999":{"type":"string"}},"anyOf":[{"required":["9999999999"]}]} -> repeat("null,", 9_999_999_999) -> ~50 GB Vec growth -> OOM abort.

Origin: byte-for-byte port of Go sjson `appendRepeat`; Go would die too. A cap is a deliberate difference and needs a docs/DIFFERENCES-FROM-GO.md entry.

Fix shape: cap the repeat count (or refuse numeric-looking keys as array indices when the path is built from a schema property name) and add a regression test with the schema above.

Windows: cargo check, fmt --check and clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings pass; workspace tests 1886 passed, the only failures are 35 that also fail at base 737ac93b plus 2 load-sensitive tests that pass alone. sjson null padding capped at 1,048,576 per edit (json.rs). title: Decide whether usage records keep full client API keys
description:
Context: cliproxy-rs-7ea.34. Every usage record (usage queue, v8 observability usage queue, the RESP usage channel, usage plugins) carries the full client key in api_key, and source falls back to it, exactly as Go v8.0.35. Collectors often ship that JSONL elsewhere, so the key travels with it.
Risk: consumers that group usage by api_key (the dashboard, external collectors, usage plugins) see a different value; Go parity of a public record shape.
Options:
A) Keep Go's record unchanged and document that usage output is secret-bearing.
B) Mask by default (first 4 and last 4 characters, as request logs do) with an opt-out; DIFFERENCES entry. Consumers lose exact-key grouping unless they opt out.
C) Add a stable keyed hash field (per process HMAC, as the cache telemetry does) alongside a masked api_key; grouping still works within a process lifetime.
Default if you say nothing: A.
Prepared: the code sites are listed on the work bead; the request-log file mode part of 7ea.34 (0644 to 0600) is being done separately as agent work.

title: Decide the replacement for unsafe-libyaml in config.yaml parsing
description:
Context: cliproxy-rs-7ea.28 split. serde_yaml_ng sits on unsafe-libyaml (unmaintained). cpa-core relies on it for config.yaml parsing and for comment-preserving v8 config rewrites that must match Go yaml.v3 byte for byte.
Risk: config.yaml compatibility with Go CLIProxyAPI for every user; a parser swap can silently change how edge-case YAML (anchors, merge keys, tags, duplicate keys) is read.
Options:
A) Wait: keep serde_yaml_ng and track its backend; accept the advisory with an audit ignore entry and a dated review.
B) Switch to serde_norway or saphyr-based serde (pure Rust, maintained), proving parity with the existing config goldens plus new edge-case fixtures recorded from Go yaml.v3.
C) Vendor unsafe-libyaml under vendor/ like gjson and maintain it (security patches by this project).
Default if you say nothing: A.
Prepared: dependency path confirmed (cargo tree: unsafe-libyaml <- serde_yaml_ng <- cpa-core <- every crate); the work bead exists with its acceptance.

title: Decide how release artifacts are signed and verified by the installers
description:
Context: cliproxy-rs-7ea.24. install.sh and install.ps1 verify the download against SHA256SUMS fetched from the same GitHub release, which proves transfer integrity but not authenticity. Anyone who can write release assets replaces both. The Homebrew tap renders from the same file. AUR and winget pin hashes in a second repo.
Risk: release infrastructure and every curl|sh / irm|iex install. AGENTS.md requires the maintainer's explicit approval to publish a release, and options B and C add a signing identity or secret.
Options:
A) Keep unsigned checksums; document the trust model in SECURITY.md and INSTALL.md, and recommend Homebrew/AUR/winget/Scoop for users who want a second source.
B) Sigstore keyless: release.yml signs SHA256SUMS with cosign using GitHub OIDC (no stored secret) and publishes SHA256SUMS.sig/.pem. Installers verify only when cosign is on PATH, and print the cosign verify command otherwise.
C) Minisign: a maintainer-held key signs SHA256SUMS in release.yml (key as an Actions secret). The public key is embedded in both installers, which verify with a small embedded verifier (PowerShell can do Ed25519 only on .NET 8+, so Windows needs a bundled helper).
Default if you say nothing: A (documentation only; no change to the release pipeline).
Prepared: the documentation text for A and the release.yml cosign step for B are drafted in the notes of cliproxy-rs-7ea.24; nothing in the release pipeline was changed.

title: Git store: no timeout on git subprocesses while holding the store lock; token re-sent on cross-host redirect; branch from remote reaches checkout without --
description:
Severity: medium.
Where: crates/cpa-store/src/git.rs
- 303-322, 487-510, 796-893: Command::output() waits indefinitely for fetch/push/clone; GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 prevents prompt hangs but not network stalls. save() runs on the management blocking thread holding the disk lock (cpa-server/src/persist.rs:19-26), so all later persists queue on self.lock.
- 296-298: the token is injected as http.extraHeader=Authorization: Basic ..., which git attaches to every request in that invocation including the first cross-host redirect it follows by default (http.followRedirects=initial). go-git goes through net/http, which strips Authorization on cross-host redirects.
- 432-459, 463-482: with GITSTORE_GIT_BRANCH unset the branch comes from ls-remote --symref and reaches `git checkout -q <target>` / `-b <target> --track origin/<target>` without `--` (a remote publishing `ref: refs/heads/--orphan` is parsed as an option). 382 `git remote add origin <remote>` also lacks `--` (operator-controlled).

Fix shape: tokio::process with a timeout and kill-on-drop; `-c http.followRedirects=false`; `--` before ref arguments and validate the symref name.

title: Release checksums are unsigned and fetched from the same release as the binary
description:
Severity: medium (supply chain).
Where: install.sh:113-122, install.ps1:64-72 fetch SHA256SUMS from the release that serves the tarball; no cosign/minisign/sigstore signature and no pinning. The Homebrew tap is rendered from the same SHA256SUMS (release.yml:213-215). AUR (packaging/aur/PKGBUILD:15-16) and winget (installer.yaml:17) pin hashes in a second repo and are stronger.

Scenario: anyone who can write release assets (leaked token, or a compromised action in the release job) replaces both files and every curl|sh / irm|iex user installs it.

Fix shape: sign SHA256SUMS (sigstore keyless from the release workflow, or a minisign key whose public half is in the installers), verify in both installers, and publish the public key in SECURITY.md.
notes:
Prepared drafts (2026-11-02) for decision cliproxy-rs-7ea.43.

Option A, documentation text for SECURITY.md / INSTALL.md:
"The install scripts check each download against SHA256SUMS from the same GitHub release. That detects a corrupted or truncated download; it does not prove the release came from the maintainer, because anyone able to replace a release asset can replace both files. If you need a second source of trust, install through Homebrew, the AUR, winget or Scoop, whose manifests pin the hashes in a separate repository."

Option B, release.yml step after SHA256SUMS is assembled (job needs permissions: id-token: write):
  - uses: sigstore/cosign-installer@<sha>   # v3
  - run: cosign sign-blob --yes --output-signature SHA256SUMS.sig --output-certificate SHA256SUMS.pem SHA256SUMS
Installer side (only when cosign is on PATH):
  cosign verify-blob --certificate SHA256SUMS.pem --signature SHA256SUMS.sig \

title: Postgres store connects outside every timeout on a single worker with an unbounded job queue
description:
Severity: medium.
Where: crates/cpa-store/src/pgconn.rs:517 `dsn.connect().await` is not under JOB_TIMEOUT; 529 connect_timeout is None unless the DSN or PGCONNECT_TIMEOUT sets one; 509 the job channel is unbounded.

Scenario: the DB host black-holes SYNs after startup; the worker hangs in connect, every later run() waits forever on its oneshot, run_blocking() (the cooldown load hook) parks a runtime thread, and the queue grows with every fire-and-forget PgCooldown::save.

Origin: Go's database/sql pool has per-call contexts.

Fix shape: wrap connect in the job timeout, default a connect_timeout, bound the channel and drop/coalesce saves when full.

description:

title: Every auth-file write (including the server's own token refresh) triggers a full auth-dir rescan and reconcile
description:
Severity: medium at scale.
Where: crates/cpa-server/src/watching.rs:462-528 `reload_config` calls scan_auth_dir (cpa-core credentials.rs:1498-1534: reads and hashes every *.json) then state.publish -> reconcile_scanned_with (see the O(C^2) reconcile bead) for any changed file, including the server's own refresh writes (new token = new hash). The log line copies Go's "processing incrementally" (watching.rs:154) but the work is a full reload. `observe` (141) does cache.0.retain(|p,_| seen.contains(p)) with seen: Vec -> quadratic per 50 ms tick while changes settle. runtime.rs:2609-2613 file writers hold reload.read() across fsync; a pending reload.write() blocks all new writers (std RwLock writer preference), so request-path persists stall during reload storms.

Needs a Go check: does v8.0.35 really reload only the single changed file? If so this is a port difference.

Fix shape: per-file upsert for a single changed path (upsert_file exists), HashSet for seen, and move the fsync out from under the reload read lock.

title: Model registry is rebuilt under a held Mutex and invalidated by every background token refresh
description:
Severity: medium.
Where: crates/cpa-server/src/runtime.rs:333-356: `self.registry` Mutex is held across store.snapshot() (Vec clone), Registry::build (cpa-core registry/dynamic.rs:1305, O(C x models)), per-credential for_executor clones and models_registered. The cache key includes store.epoch(), which apply_patch_with (2573) and admit_codex_refresh (2426) bump on every refresh commit. route() and run_routed each call rt.registry() (dispatch.rs:705, 961, 974).

Scenario: 2,000 OAuth credentials refreshing hourly -> ~33 rebuilds a minute, each blocking every concurrent request on the Mutex. No deadlock (no lookup_model re-entry on the build path), contention only.

Fix shape: build outside the lock and compare-and-swap (ArcSwap or Mutex<Option<Arc>> with a build generation), and do not bump the registry epoch for metadata-only patches that cannot change the catalog.

title: Scheduler and reconcile paths scan flat maps per credential under the store/scheduler locks (O(C^2))
description:
Severity: medium at 2,000 accounts (a supported case; bench/idle.sh tests it).
Where:
- crates/cpa-server/src/scheduler.rs:1711-1765 `records` filters the whole flat cooldowns map per credential; runtime.rs:1829-1834 calls it for every credential on every persist (O(C x K)).
- scheduler.rs:1919-1925 `reconcile` and 1908-1917 `clear_disabled`: `credentials.iter().any` inside retains over cooldowns, affinity groups (up to 65,536), LCP groups (4,096) and probes; runtime.rs:1929-1950 `clear_replaced_unauthorized` is `before.iter().find` per after credential. All under inner.write() + reload.write(). refresh.rs:100-103 already uses a HashSet.
- scheduler.rs:1345-1349, 1406-1414, 1507-1513, 1666-1689, 1694-1701: per-failure bookkeeping walks the whole flat cooldowns map.
- runtime.rs:1150-1160 `ready` per acquire: Vec `exclude.contains`, provider_keys cloned per credential (1335-1337), key String allocations; dispatch.rs:1093-1182 re-acquires per attempt so a provider-wide 5xx round costs C^2/2 compares.
- dispatch.rs:1003-1026 clones the store snapshot twice and `pinned_exclusion.contains` in a loop.

Origin: Go keeps per-auth model state maps; the port flattened them.

Fix shape: index cooldowns by credential id (nested map), HashSet for exclude/attempted/ids, precompute provider_keys once per selection.

title: cpa-exec gemini.rs deep_stack: fixed 1 GiB thread, expect() on spawn failure, ignores brackets in strings
description:
Severity: medium.
Where: crates/cpa-exec/src/gemini.rs:168-203. Unlike cpa_translate::deep_stack (crates/cpa-translate/src/lib.rs:621-648), which sizes the stack per level, returns an error when the reservation fails and guards against nested spawns, this duplicate spawns a fixed 1 GiB stack for anything nested > 256 and `.expect("deep JSON translation thread")`s the spawn. Its depth counter skips brackets inside strings, so JSON schemas carried inside string fields are not counted. Used by Gemini, AI Studio, Antigravity and Vertex; gemini_schema's own recursive passes (gemini_schema.rs:120-132 only spawn a big thread when the literal "$ref" is present) rely on it from antigravity_request.rs:333-365, kimi.rs:1121, xai_request.rs:697,963.

Scenario: a client sends [[[[... 300 deep on a memory-limited host (cgroup, ulimit -v, overcommit off): spawn fails and the task panics instead of answering 400; many such requests reserve 1 GiB each of address space.

Fix shape: delete this copy and call cpa_translate::deep_stack (or move the shared one to cpa-common). The module comment already marks it ponytail.

title: Windows: UNIX_EPOCH + Duration panics on millisecond-scale resets_at from Codex/Meta 429 bodies
description:
Severity: medium (Windows builds only; panics the request task).
Where: crates/cpa-exec/src/codex_response.rs:138 and crates/cpa-exec/src/meta.rs:548: `UNIX_EPOCH + Duration::from_secs(at as u64)` uses the panicking Add. On Windows SystemTime stores 100 ns FILETIME intervals in an i64, so checked_add fails once seconds exceed ~9.2e11 and Add panics ("overflow when adding duration to instant"). Linux/macOS timespec adds fine.

Scenario: a Codex 429 body {"error":{"type":"usage_limit_reached","resets_at":1762000000000}} (13-digit millisecond timestamp) panics the request on the winget-packaged build.

Origin: Go's time.Unix never panics. quota.rs:266-287 already does this right with checked_add.

Fix shape: use checked_add and treat overflow as "unknown reset"; clamp like quota.rs MAX_WINDOW. Also unbounded Duration producers at codex_response.rs:147, devin.rs:176, openai_compat_payload.rs:812 (currently safe because consumers use checked_add).

title: Claude relay line splitter rescans the partial line from byte zero on every chunk (quadratic)
description:
Severity: medium.
Where: crates/cpa-exec/src/claude/stream.rs:168-188 `chunk`: `self.line.extend_from_slice(chunk)` then `self.line.iter().position(|b| *b == b'\n')` from offset 0. MAX_LINE allows 50 MiB. `proxy::lines` (crates/cpa-exec/src/proxy.rs:1364-1430) does this correctly with a `scanned` cursor.

title: config.yaml is truncated and rewritten in place, not written via temp file + rename
description:
Severity: medium.
Where: crates/cpa-core/src/config/document.rs:636-647 `ConfigDocument::write` uses create(true).truncate(true); it follows symlinks and mode(0o600) only applies to a new file. Called by Config::load_text secret hashing (config.rs:994) and every v8 config PUT (management.rs:1173). Credential files, by contrast, use write_bytes_atomic correctly.

Scenario: crash or disk-full between truncate and write_all -> empty or partial config; on restart the proxy runs with no client keys and no management hash.

Origin: Go's os.WriteFile behaves the same.

Fix shape: reuse write_bytes_atomic (exclusive-create 0600 temp, sync_all, rename) and preserve the existing file's mode. DIFFERENCES entry.

description:

title: Windows: drive-relative credential name escapes auth-dir in management download
description:
Severity: medium (authenticated management caller, Windows only).
Where: crates/cpa-server/src/management/auth_files.rs:275-277 `unsafe_name` rejects only `/` and `\`; 812-822 `download` does `auth_dir.join(&name)`. On Windows PathBuf::push replaces self when the pushed path has a drive prefix but no root (`C:x.json`). Upload and delete are safe (they take `Path::new(name).file_name()`, 882-886 and 1174-1177).

Scenario: GET /v8/management/credentials/download?name=C:config.json -> reads the per-drive cwd-relative file, any `.json` on that drive.

Origin: Go's filepath.Join keeps `C:\auth\C:x.json` (an ADS inside auth-dir), so this is a port defect.

Fix shape: use the same file_name() normalisation as upload/delete, and reject names containing `:` or any Prefix component. The same `unsafe_name` is used at 1117 and 1171; check those too.

title: Key-less requests count toward the per-IP ban; with CORS * a web page can lock 127.0.0.1 out for 30 min
description: Severity: medium (availability). Where: crates/cpa-server/src/management/access.rs:225-228 (empty key counts as a failure), 177-182 (fifth failure bans the IP), 200-215 (ban checked first), 347-349 (Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *). Scenario: a malicious page the operator visits embeds five times (simple GET, no preflight). Client IP is 127.0.0.1, so the remote-disabled branch does not short-circuit; each request hits provided.is_empty() -> fail(ip). Loopback is banned for 30 min: the signed-in dashboard, the TUI and every local client get 403. Origin: same middleware in Go handler.go. Also: Access-Control-Allow-Headers: * re-opens cross-origin key use via X-Management-Key (access.rs:261-280, 349); version headers are added to 401/403 so any origin can fingerprint the server. Fix shape: do not count key-less requests, or skip counting when Sec-Fetch-Site says cross-site; list allowed headers explicitly. Needs a DIFFERENCES entry.

title: Loopback reverse proxy makes every remote caller 'local' for management auth
description:
Severity: medium, deployment-dependent.
Where: crates/cpa-server/src/management/access.rs:136-155, 217-233; crates/cpa-core/src/config/trusted.rs:161-175. `local` is client_ip == 127.0.0.1/::1; with no server.trusted-proxies the forwarded headers are ignored, so a proxy on loopback (cloudflared, nginx) makes remote callers local: allow-remote: false no longer applies and the `--password` local password is accepted. A set MANAGEMENT_PASSWORD also implicitly turns allow_remote on (line 217). The code warns once.

Scenario: proxy on 127.0.0.1 in front of the server, management.allow-remote: false, started with --password x -> anyone on the internet authenticates with x or bypasses the remote-disabled check.

Origin: identical gin behaviour in Go.

Fix shape: document prominently in GETTING-STARTED/MULTI-ACCOUNT, and consider refusing to start the local-password path when a proxy is detected (e.g. X-Forwarded-For present from loopback without trusted-proxies) rather than warning once.

description:

title: Request-log capture buffers the whole body with no cap before client auth
description:
Severity: medium (only with observability.logs.request-log: true).
Where: crates/cpa-server/src/request_logging.rs:131-150: when `enabled`, `axum::body::to_bytes(body, usize::MAX)` runs in the capture layer, which main.rs:1367 installs outside the app and therefore before `access::require_client_key`. The 64 MiB `DefaultBodyLimit` (lib.rs:140) governs extractors only; nothing caps this read unless `server.max-request-body-bytes` (off by default) is set.

Scenario: request logging on, unauthenticated POST /v1/messages with chunked transfer-encoding and a multi-GiB body -> whole body on the heap, then 401. N parallel connections -> OOM.

Origin: Go's logging middleware also io.ReadAll's with no cap, but this silently defeats the Rust-only 64 MiB ceiling the project documents.

Fix shape: apply MAX_REQUEST_BYTES (or the configured limit) to the eager read, or move capture inside the auth layer for inference routes.

title: HTTP/1 listener has no hyper timer: header-read timeout dropped, no idle timeout (slowloris)
description:
Severity: medium.
Where: crates/cpa-server/src/listener.rs:306 `hyper::server::conn::http1::Builder::new()` with no `.timer(TokioTimer::new())`. hyper 1.11.1 (Cargo.lock) drops its default 30 s `header_read_timeout` with a warning when no timer is set. Only the 10 s sniff/handshake deadline (listener.rs:73,156-170) covers the first byte. No connection cap either.

Scenario: attacker opens thousands of sockets, sends one byte, then one byte a minute; each holds a tokio task, a socket and hyper state until the attacker leaves.

Fix shape: set `.timer(hyper_util::rt::TokioTimer::new())`, keep `header_read_timeout`, consider an idle keep-alive timeout and a connection semaphore. Check what Go CLIProxyAPI sets on its http.Server before deciding the values.

title: deep_stack 1 GiB clamp: legitimate bracket-heavy traffic reserves 1 GiB per request; AnyValue has no explicit-stack decoder
description:
Severity: medium (plausible), not confirmed by measurement.
Where: crates/cpa-translate/src/lib.rs:621-648 size = levels x 8 KiB clamped to 1 GiB, so the guarantee ends at 131,072 levels; Depth (553-596) counts every [ and { inside strings and Framed::event (stream.rs:394) accumulates them for the life of a stream.
(a) A prompt or streamed code response with >131k brackets makes every request/event spawn a thread with a 1 GiB stack reservation; where mmap fails (overcommit=2, ulimit -v, small containers) the request or the rest of the stream fails.
(b) Above the clamp a walker that truly recurses can still overflow: AnyValue::from_res (json.rs:2820-2838) on a client tool schema at openai_claude.rs:119 (also 301, openai_responses.rs:653,939,1118, gemini_schema.rs:1250); GoValue got iterative decode/write/drop (json.rs:2923-3212) but AnyValue did not.
(c) hooks::normalize_tracked and translate_request plugin hooks (lib.rs:444-480) run on the worker stack after deep_stack.

Fix shape: count brackets outside strings only (as the validator does), give AnyValue the explicit-stack treatment, and consider a hard nesting refusal (400) above the 10,000-level validator cap instead of a bigger stack.

title: OAuth web forwarder writes raw request-target bytes into the Location header
description:
